Definition: a murmuring sound, i.e. a musical notation (probably similar to the modern affettuoso to indicate solemnity of movement); by implication, a machination
BiblicalUsage: higgâyôwn — a murmuring sound, a musical meditation. That is the whole of it, and it is enough: 4 occurrences, and in Psalms and Lamentations the meaning never wavers. I keep coming back to the simple reading because the simple reading is the true one.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe higgâyôwn matters because meditation is the quiet work of letting God’s word sink in. I hold that the simple reading is the true one, and I will not trade it for a clever one.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
